name: Ega
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 6 other works consulted do not discuss stress.
catalog_citation: Connell, Bruce, Firmin Ahoua & Dafydd Gibbon. 2002. Ega. Journal of the International Phonetic Association 32(1): 99-104 (Illustrations of the IPA). doi:10.1017/S002510030200018X
catalog_quote: Ega is a register tone language with three basic level tones, High (H), Mid (M) and Low (L). Tone functions both lexically and grammatically. Examples of the three tones are: nI ta 'I speak' / nI ta 'I spoke' / nI ta 'I chew' [tone diacritics on ta not preserved in]. Tonal contours come about through a number of different processes. First, tones may combine on monosyllables to give contours of HM, HL, MH through synchronic or diachronic processes of vowel deletion, leaving the unassociated tone to dock on a preceding or following vowel ... Other contours arise through the effect of the voiced series of plosives which act as depressor consonants (see below): following M and H tones are realized with a rise ... Tones following non-depressor consonants are level, other things being equal. ... Tone realization at a more global (phrasal) level appears to be relatively uninfluenced by declination. There does appear to be some form of lowering, which we refer to as automatic downstep, however, detailed work to understand the true nature and motivation of this downtrend is only in the initial stages.
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

The quoted passage is present verbatim: p.102 section 'Tone' opens 'Ega is a register tone language with three basic level tones, High (H), Mid (M) and Low (L). Tone functions both lexically and grammatically. Examples of the three tones are: nI ta..'; the second half of the quote is on p.103 after Table 2: 'Tone realization at a more global (phrasal) level appears to be relatively unin-fluenced by declination. There does appear to be some form of lowering, which we refer to as automatic downstep, however..' (only difference is the line-break hyphe…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Ega is described purely as a three-level (H/M/L) register/terraced tone language; none of the accessible first-hand descriptions (Connell et al. 2002 JIPA; Bole-Richard 1983 sketch grammar; Bôle-Richard 2006; Gibbon et al. 2002; Gibbon 2022, 2024) posits word stress or a word accent, nor do they explicitly deny one. Corroborating quote, Bole-Richard 1983 §3.1: 'L'Ega a trois tons ponctuels haut/moyen/bas qu'on met aisément en évidence' (Ega has three level tones high/mid/low, easily demonstrated).
new_statements.exceptions: None regarding stress. Tonal details only: contours arise from vowel deletion and from depressor consonants (/b d ɟ g gb v z/) which make following M and H rise; noun-class prefixes are L before a depressor; Gibbon et al. 2002 note no vowel-length contrast 'except in isolated words such as /ˈfeː̃/ all' (the ˈ there is a transcription mark, not a stress claim).
new_statements.domain_note: Tone illustrated on words and short clauses (nI ta 'I speak/spoke/chew'); phrasal level shows automatic downstep/terracing (Connell et al. 2002; Gibbon 2022 'terraced tone language.. not intonation in the conventional sense'). Speakers from Gniguédougou and Gnama, same dialect area.
new_statements.identity_note: All sources describe Ega proper (glottocode egaa1242, ISO ega), Divo Department. Connell et al. 2002 speakers are from Gniguédougou and Gnama (stated to be the same dialect area); Bole-Richard 1983 covers the language as a whole (21 villages in 3 groups) and Gibbon's later work is also Gniguédougou-based. No sub-dialect glottocodes exist.

tone_statements.citation: Gibbon, Dafydd, Bruce Connell & Firmin Ahoua (content). 2005 [last updated 14 June 2006]. E-MELD School of Best Practices: Ega Phonology (Ega case study; companion page: About Ega, Glottolog ref 670310). The LINGUIST List / E-MELD. Online:http://emeld.org/school/case/ega/phonology.html(site retired; Internet Archive capture of 16 July 2010).
tone_statements.quote: Ega has ATR vowel harmony, and three discrete level register tones (low, mid and high). There are no coda consonants in Ega, and onsets may be complex: i.e. syllables in Ega are one of V, CV or CCV. Tone in Ega is morphosyntactic, and marks tense on verbs: ta_H : I speak ta_M : I have spoken However, these underlying tones may surface differently in the context of certain consonants. For example, high vowels in syllables with voiced onsets surface with a rising tone: / E_BgU_H / [EgU_R ] canary
tone_statements.locator: section 'Harmony and tones' (first section of the page); identical text in the 2005-2010 captures listed by CDX
tone_statements.n_tones: 3 (L, M, H); rising surface contour conditioned by voiced onsets

tone_statements.citation: Gibbon, Dafydd. 2002. Computational phonology and the typology of West African tone systems. In Ulrike Gut & Dafydd Gibbon (eds.), Typology of African Prosodic Systems (Bielefeld Occasional Papers on Typology 1), 13-27. Bielefeld: Universität Bielefeld. [proceedings of TAPS 2001; author's PDF]
tone_statements.quote: What of systems with more than two tones? An example of such a system is Ega, which Ahoua, Connell and I are examining in our current project "Ega: a documentation model for an endangered Ivorian language". Ega has been analysed as a three-tone language. Following the - possibly perceptually motivated - preference for discrete level tone systems if there are more than two tones, high demi-terraces in Ega are on the same pitch, without automatic downstep, and low demi-terraces are also on the same low pitch.
tone_statements.locator: pp. 18-19, section 5 'Explanatory adequacy revisited: Comparing FS models of tone systems'

tone_statements.citation: Bole-Richard, Rémy. 1983. La classification nominale en Ega. Journal of West African Languages 13(1): 51-62.
tone_statements.quote: Sa phonologie présente quelques caractéristiques intéressantes: ... e) Existence de 3 tons ponctuels Haut, Moyen, Bas, qui sont stables mais dont la réalisation est conditionnée par la consonne qui précède = modulation des tons non-Bas après les sonores fortes / b, v, d, z, ɟ, g, gb /. ... La marque de classe des noms est une voyelle préfixée, à ton bas ou moyen (conditionnement phonologique).
tone_statements.translation: Its phonology shows some interesting features: ... e) Existence of 3 level tones High, Mid, Low, which are stable but whose realisation is conditioned by the preceding consonant = modulation (contouring) of non-Low tones after the fortis voiced consonants /b, v, d, z, ɟ, g, gb/. ... The class marker of nouns is a prefixed vowel, with low or mid tone (phonologically conditioned).
tone_statements.locator: p.53, sec.1 Présentation point (e) and sec.2
tone_statements.summary: Noun-class article; p.53 states three level tones H, M, L, non-Low tones contoured after fortis voiced obstruents; noun prefix Low, raised to Mid before a non-Low tone (p.55). Nothing on stress.
